summary: Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993. She taught Qian Lin and took up a post at the University of Washington around 1995.

Ana Agud is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Salamanca and the University of Tübingen. Around 1989, she served as Professor in the Department De Filologia Clasica e Indoeuropeo at the University of Salamanca.

Anagarika Dharmapala was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, St. Benedict's College, S. Thomas' College (~1878–1883), and Royal College (~1883). He founded the Maha Bodhi Society and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda studied at Naples, Cagliari, and Freiburg, as well as under traditional teachers. Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, he taught at Visva-Bharati, Patna, and other universities, and served as Ācārya of Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933–1985).

Anagarika Munindra, active in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Satya Narayan Goenka and Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966). He served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957 and taught Joseph Goldstein, Sharon Salzberg, and Dipa Ma.

Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche. He served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Ananda Guruge studied Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon (BA 1947) and earned a PhD from the University of London. He held posts at NIEPA (attested 1970), CSU Fullerton, and University of the West (attested 2012).

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy studied at Wycliffe College and University College London under Caroline Rhys Davids. Working in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, he directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon and held curatorial and research posts at the MFA Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indologist and historian. He served as professor at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), chairman of the Numismatic Society of India (1947), professor at Patna University (~1949–1957), and director of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1950–1959).

Anantalal Thakur, an Indologist and philosopher, studied at the University of Calcutta under teachers including Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and Satkari Mookerjee. He held professorships at the Mithila Institute (attested 1957–1987) and directed the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, University of Leeds (~1978–1984), and under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, serving as professor of religion at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

Andrea Acri studied Indology and religious studies, completing a PhD at Leiden University (~2006–2011) under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen. He served as a junior researcher at Leiden and became maître de conférences at EPHE in 2016.

Andrea R. Jain studied at SMU (2002–2004) and Rice University (PhD 2004–2010). Specializing in religious studies and Indology, she held adjunct roles at Houston and Rice before advancing from assistant to full professor at Indiana University (2010–2021).
Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed both a Master's degree (by 2008) and a PhD (by 2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

Andreas Doctor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, and studied under traditional teachers including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, Neten Chokling Rinpoche, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche.
Andreas Spengel was a scholar in linguistics who studied at the University of Munich and the University of Berlin. During his career, he taught Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol. Messent's doctoral supervisor was Paul Williams, and Messent also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov was a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky) and later taught Bidia Dandaron.

Andrew B. Irvine is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from Boston University. He held an appointment as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett is a linguist who studied at Harvard University from approximately 1983 to 1990. He took up a post at the University of California, Berkeley around 1995.
